draft.title: Compensatory damages
card: Compensatory damages are a sum of money paid by the defendant to the plaintiff. They aim to make up for the loss the plaintiff suffered because of the wrong.
money lost or spent because of the wrong, such as medical bills, repair costs and wages the plaintiff could not earn.
harm that has no price tag, such as pain and suffering, loss of enjoyment of life and emotional distress.
The plaintiff must show the loss. A court sets an amount that it thinks fairly covers it. The aim is to compensate, not to punish the defendant.
draft.remember: Compensatory damages pay for the plaintiff's loss, both money lost and pain suffered.

a.q: Which best describes the purpose of compensatory damages?
opts: To make up for the loss the plaintiff suffered
To punish the defendant for how they behaved
To stop the defendant repeating the wrong
To show the claim was a waste of time
a.why: Compensatory damages are paid to make up for the plaintiff's loss. Punishing the defendant is tempting, but that is not the aim of compensatory damages: they compensate, not punish.
a.clue: Think about who the money is meant to help.

b.q: Priya is hurt when a delivery van driven carelessly hits her car in Ballarat. She wins her case. Which part of her claim is for non-economic loss?
opts: The pain and distress she suffered from her injuries
The cost of repairing her damaged car
The wages she lost while off work
The hospital bills she paid after the crash
b.why: Pain and distress cannot be measured by a bill, so they are non-economic loss. Repair costs, lost wages and hospital bills are all money lost or spent, so they are economic loss.
b.clue: Which loss has no receipt or pay slip behind it?

a.best: To make up for the loss the plaintiff suffered

b.best: The pain and distress she suffered from her injuries
